headline: 13.54% of university graduates are unemployed in Bangladesh, highest among all education levels
summary: Latest labor force survey reveals nearly 885,000 highly educated individuals are jobless, highlighting a stark reality where advanced degrees increase unemployment risk.
details: Bangladesh faces a severe graduate unemployment crisis, with 13.54% of university graduates currently jobless, the highest rate across all education levels. This translates to approximately 885,000 highly educated individuals struggling to find work.

In stark contrast, the unemployment rate for individuals without any formal education stands at a mere 1.25%. This data suggests a troubling trend where the pursuit of higher institutional education in Bangladesh paradoxically increases the risk of unemployment.

The statistics reflect daily struggles for many, like Asif, a former Jagannath University student in Narinda, Old Dhaka, who worries about rent and job hunting two years post-graduation. Tanvir in Rajabazar faces challenges covering daily expenses and commute costs, while Roni from Rangpur, who travels to Dhaka for exams, has accumulated two months of outstanding mess rent and grocery bills.

Experts note these individuals represent millions of unemployed youth. Annually, around 700,000 graduates enter the job market, but only about 300,000 institutional jobs are created. Securing a government job, like through BCS or bank recruitment, can take 3-5 years from preliminary exams to final recommendation.

Professor Ridwanul Haque of IBA, Dhaka University, identifies a major mismatch between educational qualifications and job market demands. He warns that in the age of AI, institutional jobs in fields like media and accounting will shrink, while technical skills will remain in high demand and grow.

To address this, he emphasizes the need to improve technical education to international standards and increase technology adoption. He also advises students to engage in internships, part-time jobs, or skill-based projects during or immediately after their studies to gain experience and overcome inertia.

According to the International Labour Organization (ILO), the unemployment rate for youth aged 18-24 in Bangladesh is 9.39%. Economists from CPD and the World Bank estimate that billions of dollars in GDP growth are lost annually due to underutilized human resources and a lack of suitable skills.

While policy reforms and curriculum changes are long-term solutions, thousands of young people in messes across the country continue their daily struggle for survival. The burden of mess rent and job application fees traps a generation's potential in a cycle of uncertainty.

headline_marked: [[6 killed in bus crash]] and 10 injured in Bogura early Friday morning
headline: 6 killed in bus crash and 10 injured in Bogura early Friday morning
summary: A bus lost control on the Bogura-Naogaon highway, hitting an electric pole and crushing workers waiting for jobs. Three died on the spot, and three more succumbed to injuries at the hospital.
details: Six people were killed and at least 10 others injured in a tragic bus accident in Bogura early Friday morning. The incident occurred in the Erulia Silkibanda area on the Bogura-Naogaon highway.
According to Bogura Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Ibrahim Ali, a bus lost control, struck an electric pole, and ran over a group of laborers who were waiting for work.
The victims were all working-class individuals and local residents, though their identities could not be immediately confirmed by the police.
The Shah Fateh Ali Paribahan bus, traveling from Dhaka to Naogaon, veered off the road around 6:30 AM. Three people died instantly at the scene of the accident.
Police, with the help of local residents, rescued the injured and transported them to Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College Hospital. There, doctors declared three more individuals dead.
